strengths: Strong empirical results with substantial improvements over prior SOTA (80.2% vs 64.2% on AndroidWorld, 53.6% vs 41.2% on AndroidLab)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with proper ablation studies (Table 3c, Figure 3b) showing contribution of each component
Outperforms much larger proprietary models (72B parameters) with smaller open models (7B/9B)
Well-executed engineering contribution: distributed framework supporting 256+ parallel Android virtual devices
Thoughtful multi-stage design with reasoning SFT providing interpretable policy initialization
Good reproducibility: open-source release, detailed hyperparameters, extensive implementation details in appendices
Clear presentation with informative architecture diagrams and result visualizations
Evaluation across multiple benchmarks (AndroidWorld, AndroidLab, AndroidControl) and backbone models
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: ADAGRPO combines known techniques (experience replay, curriculum learning, reward shaping) without fundamental innovation
Reward model bias for AndroidLab: VLM-based reward model achieves only 86% accuracy; authors acknowledge bias from proprietary VLM majority voting
Best model (MOBILERL-9B) trained only on AndroidWorld while MOBILERL-7B trained on both, suggesting different configurations for different benchmarks
Narrow evaluation scope: Android-only, no evaluation on real public-use apps (acknowledged limitation), relatively small benchmarks (20 and 9 apps)
XML-based grounding is fundamental limitation: many popular apps lack sufficient accessibility information; eventually requires visual-only grounding (unaddressed)
Substantial resource requirements severely limit reproducibility: requires 4 CPU machines with 1TB memory, 256 parallel rollouts, 25+ hours for 100 training steps
Heavy dependence on SFT initialization: reasoning-free SFT alone provides +22.6% improvement, dominating RL gains of +15.2%
SPA shows smallest impact in ablations (+1.9% on AndroidWorld), with primary benefit in step efficiency rather than accuracy
Ad-hoc FCF design: threshold selection (2 consecutive failures, 3-epoch cooldown) lacks principled justification
Missing error analysis and limited discussion of which task types benefit from which components
